title: How have the protests in France changed?
description:
Protests are still ongoing across France, but now it’s no longer just about schools. People of all ages are protesting over a high cost of living. But there was violence and riots over the weekend, with thousands of arrests.

Dramatic pictures of wreckage, fires and police clampdowns have spread online and have had a huge response internationally. But what exactly is happening and why have things shifted since earlier protests this month? We hear from BBC reporter Pierre-Antoine Denis, about what has caused this intense shift.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討法國抗議活動如何從最初針對學校設施劣化與教師不足的學生示威，升級為涵蓋各年齡層對高生活成本及總統馬克宏政府的不滿。 BBC 記者皮埃爾—安東尼·德尼指出，「黃背心」運動已與學生結盟，部分抗議者因認為多年和平遊行無果而轉向暴動與搶劫，迫使政府在巴黎、尼斯等城市實施宵禁，而社群媒體上流傳的暴力與警方執法影片更加劇了警民對立。
summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, presenter Iqra Farooq and BBC reporter Pierre-Antoine Denis examine how French protests have shifted from student-led demonstrations over poor school infrastructure into a widespread movement. People of all ages are now protesting against the high cost of living and expressing deep discontent with President Emmanuel Macron's administration. As the Yellow Vests joined forces with students, parts of the protests escalated into rioting, looting, and violence, leading authorities to impose curfews in cities like Paris and Nice. Viral social media footage of both destruction and police violence has further heightened public tension and anger.

Yes, so these protests at the core, obviously, is still about these students and their demands for better funding and more consideration towards the education system in the country.

But it's obviously so important and and crucial to make a distinction between the violence and the overwhelming amount of protest that ended up being completely peaceful and with messaging or just with people walking around with with placards and and just showcasing their anger and their discontent.
Yeah, like you were saying, we've seen those smashed shop windows, the shattered glass on the streets.
And I think these is these are the pictures and the images that really shocked the nation of France and and the French population.
Police officers patrolling the streets, if they are thinking that you could be a minor, they would want to ask for your ID.
